memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Sarah was afraid, so she lied and said, "I did not laugh." But he said, "Yes, you did laugh." - Gen 18:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Caught out, Sarah is afraid - and fear makes her lie. "I did not laugh." But God, gently and firmly, will not let the pretence stand: "Yes, you did laugh." He does not accept her cover-up, but neither does He crush her. He simply speaks the truth.

There is something profoundly freeing in this exchange. Sarah tried to hide, as we all do. When we are caught in our doubt, our sin, or our failure, our instinct is to deny, to minimise, to pretend. Fear whispers that we must cover ourselves. But God already knows. Our pretending fools no one, least of all Him.

And notice what God does not do. He does not thunder in anger or withdraw His promise because Sarah lied. He states the truth plainly - "Yes, you did laugh" - and then, remarkably, the promise still stands. Her fear-driven lie did not cancel God's grace.

This is the God we can be honest with. There is no point hiding from the One who sees everything, and no need to, because His grace is greater than our failures. "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us" (1 John 1:9). Honesty before God is always better than hiding. He already knows the truth about you - and He loves you still. Stop pretending, and come to Him as you really are.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you hiding something from God that He already knows?
- Can you come to God honestly, trusting His grace is greater than your failure?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You see the truth about me, and there is no use hiding. Forgive me for pretending. Help me come to You honestly, as I really am, trusting that Your grace is greater than my failures.
Amen.
